name: cyclic-annulus-sector
reference: Benchmark F4e (#81). Lame thick cylinder, a = 0.1 m, b = 0.2 m, internal pressure p = 60 MPa, E = 200 GPa, nu = 0.3, the same closed form lame-axisymmetric and lame-3d-revolve-hex20 use: A = p a^2/(b^2 - a^2) = 20 MPa, B = p a^2 b^2/(b^2 - a^2) = 8e5 Pa m^2, sigma_theta(a) = 100 MPa, sigma_rr(a) = -60 MPa whatever the idealisation. This row is the same 8 x 2 (r, z) strip as lame-3d-revolve-hex20 revolved 60 degrees in 10 hex20 segments instead of 90 in 16, and tied to itself with constraint.cyclic between the revolve mesher's theta0 and theta1 Sets instead of a symmetry plane, because 60 degrees does not land on a coordinate axis the way 90 does. Unlike lame-3d-revolve-hex20 there is no uz = 0 on the end faces here: theta1 is entirely a slave of the cyclic tie, and its edge nodes coincide with zmin/zmax, so fixing those faces would collide with the tie's own rows (constraint.conflict) -- the schema has no way to name 'this face except that edge'. Instead a single node on theta0 (a master, never a slave) is pinned in its tangential (uy) and axial (uz) components, which removes the tie's two remaining freedoms (translation along the axis, and rotation about it -- the only motion the tie itself does not already force to zero) without conflict. Leaving both ends free gives the free-ends Lame variant, u_r(a) = 5.90e-5 m, which is BENCHMARKS.md's C2 row's own SimScale number, not an invented one. Measured: sigma_theta(a) = 99.847585 MPa (0.15 %), sigma_rr(a) = -59.685569 MPa (0.52 %), u_r(a) = 5.900002e-5 m (0.0003 %).
